title: Strawberry Spinach Smoothie
subtitle: Green · Green
description: Strawberry-banana sweetness hides the spinach completely. A good first step when the hall wants to eat better without a lecture.
intro: Strawberry-banana sweetness hides the spinach completely. A good first step when the hall wants to eat better without a lecture.

steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Strawberry Spinach Smoothie in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Blend. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

Blend spinach with milk first until smooth — no visible leaves. Serve cold within 10 minutes — hold blended cups on ice at 38°F if the line runs long. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

Add strawberries, banana, and yogurt. Blend until thick and pink, not brown. Serve cold within 10 minutes — hold blended cups on ice at 38°F if the line runs long. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

Stir in chia at the end if using, or blend 10 seconds on low. Serve cold within 10 minutes — hold blended cups on ice at 38°F if the line runs long. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

Drink within a few hours; chia will thicken if it sits overnight. Serve cold within 10 minutes — hold blended cups on ice at 38°F if the line runs long. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

substitutions: Flax meal (1 tbsp) instead of chia.
shiftNote: Easy sell to crews skeptical of green food — looks and tastes like a berry shake.
